Stalls are earned, never bought: your rank grants 2 at Noble and 1 more per rank gained (6 at King), each owned horse-pasture region grants 3 (6 such pastures exist), and each stable district building grants 1 (up to 12).
Foals in training. Set each horse's training focus, manage its fatigue, answer stable events, and break it in when ready.
Your broken-in horses. Assign them as mounts, sell them, dedicate them to your armies, breed them, or turn them loose.

Rest clears 30 fatigue per turn. A tired horse (50+) risks training setbacks; an exhausted one (80+) risks them badly.
The horse's current training. It keeps at this until you change it - pick a focus with the round buttons below.
Age in turns, with turns remaining in brackets - at the cap the horse is broken in whether you are ready or not. Fatigue past 50 risks setbacks; past 80, serious ones. Rest to recover.

Total training decides the quality at break-in: 30+ Refined, 55+ Exceptional, 80+ Elite, with a small chance to land one tier higher or lower. A bought foal tops out around Exceptional - Elite comes from breeding.
End this horse's training now. Its highest aptitude picks the bloodline, its total training the quality, and it moves to the paddock. Needs paddock room.
A stable event concerning this horse is waiting in your event feed. Answer it there; the horse keeps training in the meantime.
Move this horse to the paddock, freeing the stall.
Sell this horse to the markets. Better horses fetch far better prices.
A broken-in horse. It stays in your paddock until you assign, sell, dedicate, breed or release it.
Born of a same-bloodline pairing. Each generation of pedigree improves this line's chance of breaking in a tier above its training.
Both parents were elite or better of the same bloodline. Champion foals are far likelier to break in a tier higher.
This horse has bred recently and must recover before pairing again.
Equip this horse on a character as their mount. A character carries one mount; any current mount returns to your Ancillaries.

Give this horse to your armies. Its bloodline grants a faction-wide blessing that scales with the horse's quality - one active per bloodline. An elite grants it permanently; a lesser horse grants it for a time, with a chance to take root forever. A permanent blessing is only replaced by a better horse of the same bloodline.
Choose this horse for breeding, then pick a mate of the opposite sex on another card. Costs 400 gold and an empty stall; the foal inherits from its parents, and same-bloodline pairs build pedigree.
Stop choosing a mate for this horse. Nothing is spent and the horse is unchanged.
This is the horse you chose to breed. Pick its mate on another card, or press Cancel.
These two are the same sex. A pairing needs a sire and a dam.
One of these horses is still recovering from a recent pairing.
Every training stall is occupied. A foal needs somewhere to be raised.
You cannot afford the breeding fee.

Pair this horse with your chosen mate for 400 gold - the foal starts training with aptitudes inherited from both parents. Greyed out when the pair cannot breed: the sexes must differ, both horses must be recovered, and you need an empty stall and the fee.

Stable a new foal here. Breeds beyond the Common foal unlock while you hold regions in their homelands, and each is born gifted in its people's signature aptitude - learning it faster and tiring slower when training it.
Click to stable this foal. Locked breeds unlock while you own a region of their homeland; the requirement is shown on the card.
